question: Should OpenClaw core define native parent/child context-pressure notification and recovery routing for saturated specialist agents, or keep this as external monitoring/plugin territory for now?
rationale: The request combines session-state monitoring with new parent identity, configurable threshold, notification target, and recovery-action semantics; repository vision cautions against default agent-hierarchy frameworks.

options.title: Define a narrow core signal
options.body: Core would expose a generic context-pressure health event for sessions/subagents and let existing channels or plugins decide how to notify operators or parents.

options.title: Keep it external for now
options.body: Maintainers would defer native parent notification and rely on custom monitoring or plugin surfaces until a broader agent hierarchy direction is accepted.

options.title: Build full parent recovery
options.body: Core would add parent identity, configurable thresholds, operator alerts, and recovery actions, accepting new config and orchestration surface.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core signal
recommendation.body: Core would expose a generic context-pressure health event for sessions/subagents and let existing channels or plugins decide how to notify operators or parents.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved part is product direction for parent-child session semantics, and steipete appears in adjacent subagent/session ownership history.
